apt-controls: An APT 600 lane is the one we meet most often on a flat staff car park. The APT 950 is the wider APT Controls entrance, and the boom is longer, so the spring and the loop positions change. Tell us which badge is on the door.
APT Controls booms are ordered to the measured opening, not to a photograph taken at an angle. If the APT 600 arm has been cut down on site, we measure what is left before a replacement is cut.
Loop tails for an APT Controls cabinet are labelled before they are lifted. A loop that was paved over is a civils conversation, not a promise made from the car park office.
When an APT Controls barrier shares a post with a pedestrian gate, the quote says whether the gate closer is included. We do not take the gate off to make the boom look straight.

Staff who use an APT 600 every morning care more about a predictable raise than about a brochure. We time three APT 600 cycles with the lane empty and write the seconds down. If an APT 950 has a skirt fitted, the skirt stays in the measurement because it changes the inertia of that longer APT arm. Paving joints over an APT loop are photographed so a later cut knows where the wire runs. The APT cabinet key is returned to the person who met us, not left in the lock.
atg-access: ATG Access work is usually a blocker or a bollard, not a lightweight parking arm. The foundation, the hydraulic pack and the rising time are the survey. A cosmetic boom swap is the wrong description for an ATG Access product.

If an ATG blocker has been left down after a power cut, we ask when it last completed a raise. The oil level, the hose and the control key are checked before anyone talks about a new ATG Access cabinet.
Pedestrian routes beside an ATG Access blocker are drawn on the note. People step around a half-raised blade. That is written as a safety point, not as a styling comment.
Spare seals and hoses for ATG Access plant are confirmed against the unit on site. We do not bring a generic car-park spring and call it an ATG part.

An ATG blocker that serves a goods yard spends its life under lorries, so the pit collects mud. We measure the mud depth before quoting an ATG seal kit. Rising time is taken with a stopwatch from the ATG control point the driver actually uses, which is sometimes a button in a hut and not the cabinet. If pedestrians have worn a path across the ATG foundation, that path is in the note as a reason to pause the test while people pass. Hydraulic leaks are traced to the hose number, not described as the whole ATG machine failing.
avon-barrier: Avon Barrier arms and Avon bollards are identified separately. A site can have both. The quote names which Avon product is being serviced so a bollard invoice is not written up as an arm.
An Avon arm that stops at forty-five degrees is often a spring, a limit, or something blocking the arc. We watch the arc with the lane empty before the Avon cabinet is condemned.
Avon bollards need a clear sleeve. Grit, a bent lid or a flooded pit is recorded with a depth, because that decides whether the Avon unit can be lifted on the day.
The Avon handover lists the key numbers the site already uses. We do not re-pin an Avon lock and take the only key away.

Avon sites often mix an arm at the car entrance with bollards at the side gate. We label the Avon arm as lane A and each Avon bollard by its pit number so the invoice cannot swap them. A bent Avon bollard lid is a separate line from a dead Avon arm motor. Residents who walk dogs through the Avon line are asked which hour is quiet enough for a test. The Avon override key is tried by the building manager while we watch, and we only adjust a limit if they agree the parked position is wrong.
dea: DEA lanes are parking operators. The call is usually a DEA cabinet that has locked the car park at the end of the day. We ask which reader or ticket machine sits beside the DEA barrier before the visit.
A DEA boom lying on the ground is made safe first. The cause, a snapped bolt or a sprung gearbox, is photographed on the DEA chassis so the replacement matches the bolt pattern.
Season tickets and free-exit loops on a DEA lane are tested with the site's own card if they will lend it. We do not invent a pass to prove the DEA reader.
DEA manuals stay with the building. If the previous maintainer took them, the note says the DEA model was identified from the plate alone.

DEA car parks usually have a pay station within sight of the arm. We stand where the driver stands, not only at the DEA door. A DEA ticket jam and a DEA arm fault are written as two jobs even when they happened on the same evening. The free-exit loop, if the DEA lane has one, is tested with a car rolling at walking pace. Night-time DEA complaints about a dark boom are passed to the lighting circuit, and we say so rather than fitting a brighter DEA LED that was not asked for.
designa: Designa is a parking system as much as a barrier. The ticket, the barrier and the exit column have to agree. A Designa arm that moves while the column rejects every ticket is a logic fault, not a spring fault.
We ask for a Designa shift report or a photograph of the rejected ticket. The time on the ticket and the time on the Designa barrier log are compared before parts are blamed.
Nesting and tariff changes are the car park operator's settings. We do not rewrite a Designa tariff. We say when the barrier is healthy and the complaint is the tariff.
A Designa lane closed with a cone is reopened only when the safety loop sees a vehicle again. The operator watches one exit with us.

Designa offices judge a lane by the shift screen, so we ask them to open that screen before we touch the Designa arm. A rejected Designa ticket is bagged and the time is copied onto the note. If the Designa column accepts the ticket and the arm still waits, the input wire is the suspect, and the Designa spring is left alone. Tariff buttons are not our job. We will say the Designa barrier is healthy when the only change the office wants is a price on the ticket.

A Designa exit that works for staff fobs and refuses visitor tickets is written as a Designa validation rule, not as a failed Designa gearbox. We ask the operator to run one known-good ticket and one rejected ticket while we watch the Designa column, and both results go on the note with the time. The Designa barrier is left in the position the car park needs overnight. We do not park a Designa arm upright to make the morning quieter unless the manager has asked for that. Power to the Designa column is identified before any cover comes off, because a dark screen and a dead arm are different faults and the quote says which one we found.

Designa lanes that share a nest with a second barrier are surveyed as a pair. A Designa arm that opens because the other lane's loop is occupied is a nesting fault, and we do not price a new Designa boom for it. The manager stands at the Designa pay station for one full exit so they can see the same screen we see. If the Designa ticket printer is out of paper, that is written as a consumable, not as a barrier repair. The free written quote names the Designa lane, the column and whether the arm itself was the fault. CAME remains the barrier partner we specify for a new lane. Designa equipment already on site is serviced or replaced. That is not a Designa partnership.
eagle: Eagle barriers on older yards often have a boom that has been tied vertically for months. We ask why it was tied. An Eagle photocell wrapped in tape is unwrapped only after the reason is written down.
The Eagle spring is matched to the boom that is fitted now, including any sign or skirt someone has added. A heavier Eagle arm needs the spring the plate allows, not the spring that was in the van.
Manual release on an Eagle cabinet is demonstrated to the person who locks the yard. They turn it. We do not leave an Eagle release that only an engineer can find.
Painted-over Eagle rating plates are cleaned enough to read the model. If the plate is gone, the Eagle gearbox casting is photographed and the quote waits for that identification.

Eagle yards on industrial estates are often locked by the last person to leave, who is not a barrier engineer. We ask that person to show the Eagle release before we service anything, because they will be the one using it at 7pm. Tape on an Eagle photocell is removed only with their say-so and the reason they taped it is written first. An Eagle boom that has lived vertically for a season may have taken a set; we say if the Eagle arm needs replacing rather than pretending a new spring will straighten it.
frontier-pitts: Frontier Pitts work may be a gate leaf, a rising arm or a vehicle blocker. Those are different foundations. The quote says which Frontier Pitts product is in the ground.
A Frontier Pitts leaf that drags is a hinge, a dropped pier or a closer, and we say which. We do not price a new Frontier Pitts leaf because the existing one scrapes.

Hostile-vehicle products from Frontier Pitts are not treated as a car-park arm. The survey includes the approach, the foundation and the duty the site thinks it has. We do not invent a rating the product does not have.
Keys and override handles for a Frontier Pitts gate are counted with the site manager. Missing Frontier Pitts keys are listed. We do not supply a lookalike padlock and call the leaf secure.

Frontier Pitts leaves are heavy. A dragging Frontier Pitts gate is a pier measurement with a tape, not a guess from the road. We record the gap under the Frontier Pitts leaf at the latch and at the hinge. Blockers in the Frontier Pitts range are quoted with the foundation that is visible, and we do not claim a security rating the casting does not show. If a Frontier Pitts closer is missing its cover, the quote includes the cover only when the manager wants it, not as a surprise extra.
heald: Heald HT1 and HT2 cabinets are easy to confuse from across the lane. We read the Heald plate at the hinge side of the door. The HT number decides the boom kit.
A Heald arm that chatters at the end of travel is adjusted on the limits, not by bending the Heald boom. The limit screws are marked before they are moved so they can be put back.
Heald loops set in block paving are tested for continuity before the paving is lifted. If the Heald loop is healthy, the fault is in the cabinet and the paving stays down.
The Heald note includes the direction of travel, in or out, because an exit Heald lane and an entry Heald lane do not share a loop setting.

Heald HT1 and Heald HT2 share a family look and not a parts list. The Heald plate is read with the door open and the characters are copied in full, including any suffix. Limits on a Heald cabinet are marked with a pencil before a screwdriver touches them, so a wrong adjustment can be undone. Block paving over a Heald loop stays put when the continuity reading is sound. Entry Heald lanes and exit Heald lanes are named on the note because their loop sensitivity is not the same setting.

A Heald boom that has been shortened on site is measured before a replacement is ordered. The Heald spring that suited the original length will not suit a cut-down arm, and we say so rather than forcing the old spring. The Heald cabinet door seal is checked because a wet Heald board is a different job from a noisy Heald gearbox. We write the Heald direction, the plate and the loop reading on one note so the next visit does not open the paving again. If the Heald arm clears cars but clips a high van, the van is the vehicle we set to, and the quote says that.

Heald parts are identified from the plate, not from a photograph taken across the car park. We do not claim a Heald partnership. CAME is the barrier partner we specify when a lane is being built new. A Heald barrier that is already in the ground is serviced or replaced on its own quote. The price is on application after the lane, the HT number and the safety devices are known. You get that quote before the Heald lane is taken out of use. The person who locks the yard is shown the Heald release, and they operate it once before we leave.
hysecurity: HySecurity equipment on these pages is the hydraulic barrier, not a sliding gate from a different range unless the plate says so. Hydraulic oil, hoses and the HySecurity motor temperature are the first checks.
A HySecurity arm that creeps down overnight is a hydraulic hold, and we measure how far it drops. That measurement is the reason a seal is quoted, not a guess from the phone call.
Cold mornings change a HySecurity raise time. We record the temperature and the seconds. A slow HySecurity raise in a frost is not automatically a failed pump.
The HySecurity manual release is a procedure, not a hidden valve for us to leave half open. The site contact operates it once while we watch.

HySecurity hydraulics are slow to forgive a low oil level. We check the HySecurity reservoir before running repeated tests, and we write the level rather than topping it up in silence. Creep is measured in millimetres over twenty minutes with the HySecurity arm at the parked angle the site uses by day. A frosty morning is noted beside the HySecurity raise time so a summer visit is not compared with a winter one unfairly. The person who will use the HySecurity manual release turns it themselves. We do not leave a valve cracked open.

Hose weep on a HySecurity cabinet is photographed against the serial plate before a seal kit is named. We do not wipe the HySecurity oil away and call the lane healthy. The HySecurity motor temperature after three raises is written next to the seconds, because a hot HySecurity motor with a normal raise is a different finding from a slow cold raise. Filters and breathers are on the quote only when they are dirty. A clean HySecurity reservoir is said to be clean.

HySecurity equipment already on a private lane is serviced or replaced. That is not a HySecurity partnership. CAME is the partner we specify when the lane is new. The HySecurity quote names the arm, the hydraulic hold and whether the safety devices still stop the boom. Price is on application after that survey. The lane is given back in the position the site uses, and the note of the oil level and the raise time stays with the building so the next HySecurity visit starts from a measurement rather than from a phone call.
life: Life SUPRA and Life GEAR operators are different machines. The Life badge and the operator cover decide which one is on the quote. A photograph of the Life cover from above is the useful one.

A Life operator that hums and does not drive the boom is isolated before the cover comes off. Capacitor and limit checks are written as readings, not as 'Life motor replaced' when the motor was not changed.
Life booms supplied with a skirt are weighed into the spring choice. Removing a Life skirt to make the arm faster is not a repair we do without saying so.
The Life handover is the cover refitted and the lane tested with a car the site provides. We do not test a Life lane by walking the loop.

Life SUPRA covers and Life GEAR covers do not interchange, so the photograph we want is square-on to the Life lid. A humming Life operator is isolated at the local switch before the lid comes off, and the readings that follow are numbers, not a story about a burnt Life motor unless the motor was actually changed. Skirts supplied with a Life boom stay on for the spring check. The test at the end is a car the site moves across the Life loop. Walking the loop is not the test we sign.
newgate: Newgate barriers on private estates are often the only control the residents trust. The Newgate arm speed is agreed with the estate, because a fast Newgate drop frightens drivers who use that entrance every day.
A Newgate lock that will not throw is the lock, the keep or the alignment of the Newgate post. We say which. Packing a Newgate keep with washers is written on the note if that is what held.
Estate fobs that release a Newgate lane are tested with a resident's fob if they offer it. We do not clone a Newgate fob.
The Newgate quote states whether the LED strip on the arm is included. A dark Newgate boom at night is a lighting fault, separate from the gearbox.

Newgate arms on housing estates are seen by the same drivers every day, so the drop speed is a conversation, not a factory default we refuse to discuss. A Newgate keep that misses the lock is measured for alignment against the Newgate post before any washer is added, and if a washer is what holds, the note says washer. Resident fobs are borrowed and handed back. We do not copy a Newgate token. A dark Newgate boom is quoted as lighting only when they ask for light, and the gearbox price is not used to hide that.
skidata: SKIDATA lanes fail in conversation between the reader and the barrier. A SKIDATA reader that beeps while the arm stays down is not diagnosed as a broken boom until the input at the SKIDATA controller is seen.
We ask the car park office for the SKIDATA device name they use on the shift screen. That name is what the note uses, so their engineer and ours are talking about the same SKIDATA lane.
Tickets jammed in a SKIDATA column are cleared and counted. A column full of tickets is an operational fault. It is not fixed by changing the SKIDATA barrier spring.
After a SKIDATA visit the office runs one entry and one exit while we watch. The SKIDATA transaction appears, or the fault is still open and the quote says so.

SKIDATA staff talk in device names from their screen. We copy that SKIDATA name onto our note before the barrier housing is opened. A SKIDATA beep with a still arm means we look at the controller input, and the boom stays on its bolts until that input has been seen. Tickets pulled from a SKIDATA column are counted and handed to the office, not binned. One entry and one exit are run by their cashier while we watch the SKIDATA transaction appear. If it does not appear, the visit stays open.

compliance-bundle: The Compliance Bundle is the published pack for one residential address: an EICR, a landlord gas safety record where gas appliances are present, and a fire risk assessment. The published price is £561. That price is the pack, not a rate for any one of the three visits on its own. Gas work inside the Compliance Bundle is carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers.

An agent booking the Compliance Bundle sends the address, the property type, whether gas is on site, and who will open the door. If the address matches the published scope, the Compliance Bundle stays at £561. If it does not, the difference is written down before anyone attends. Nothing is added on the day.

The Compliance Bundle file comes back as one set for that address. The EICR lists what was inspected. The gas safety record, where the property has gas, lists the appliances that were checked. The fire risk assessment names the actions. Remedial electrical work, unsafe appliances and fire actions are quoted separately. They are not folded into the £561.

A property with no gas appliances is outside the published Compliance Bundle. We quote the EICR and the fire risk assessment without describing a gas record as included. Tell us that on the form. The Compliance Bundle is also not the Let Ready package. Let Ready stays price on application and can include other certificates.

The Compliance Bundle is booked from 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, Stockport SK2 5DE. Call or WhatsApp 07517 806082 or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com. Same-day and next-day visits are offered when the diary allows. The written confirmation itemises VAT. You keep the three records with the property file.

Use the Compliance Bundle when one home needs those three records together and the scope matches the published pack. A shop, a house in multiple occupation outside the stated scope, or a block of flats is a different instruction. We say so and quote that building on its own. The Compliance Bundle page is the page for the published £561 pack.

The Compliance Bundle confirmation names the address and the three records. If a second building is mentioned in the same email, it is not silently added to the Compliance Bundle. Each address is its own Compliance Bundle booking or its own written quote.

After the Compliance Bundle papers are emailed, questions about a code on the report are answered against that report. We do not rewrite a failed item into a pass. A follow-on repair is a new instruction with its own price, not a line discovered on the Compliance Bundle invoice.

An agent using the Compliance Bundle is usually collecting a file for a landlord who will not attend. The Compliance Bundle email therefore names the agent and the landlord separately, and the records are addressed so the agent can forward them without rewriting our sentences. If two Compliance Bundle homes are booked for the same morning, each keeps its own £561 confirmation. We do not merge two Compliance Bundle addresses onto one report because the keys were on the same ring.

The Compliance Bundle survey starts with the consumer unit, then the appliances if gas is present, then the escape routes the fire risk assessment has to describe. That order is how the Compliance Bundle day is planned so the household is not walking surveyors past each other. Questions about a code are answered from the Compliance Bundle report that was emailed, and a fail stays a fail.
landlord-pack: The Landlord pack is the same published £561 offer, written for the landlord who is turning a tenancy over on one home. It is an EICR, a landlord gas safety record where the home has gas appliances, and a fire risk assessment. It is not a price list for odd jobs. Gas work in the Landlord pack is carried out by Gas Safe registered engineers.

A landlord booking the Landlord pack tells us whether the house is empty or occupied, who pays, and whether a tenant has to give access. We do not arrive unannounced. If the home matches the published scope, the Landlord pack stays at £561. If a loft conversion, a house-share or a missing gas supply takes it outside that scope, you get the difference in writing first.

After the Landlord pack visit the landlord can send the file to the agent. The EICR is the electrical report for that home. The gas record lists the appliances that were checked. The fire risk assessment is the note for that address. C1 or C2 electrical items, an unsafe appliance and actions from the assessment are their own quotes. They are not inside the £561.

If the let has no gas, say so. The Landlord pack as published expects the gas record where appliances are present. A gas-free home is quoted as the electrical report and the fire risk assessment only. We do not print a gas certificate that was not earned. The Landlord pack is not a promise to redecorate, to change a consumer unit, or to licence an HMO.

Book the Landlord pack from the Stockport office at 17 Woodlands Park Road, Offerton, SK2 5DE. Phone 07517 806082, WhatsApp the same number, or email icomplypropertyservices@gmail.com. The date is agreed around the tenant. Certificates are emailed so they can sit with the tenancy papers.

Choose the Landlord pack when the instruction is a single home and a change of tenancy, and the three records are what the agent has asked for. A commercial unit, a block, or a portfolio priced as one job is not this page. Those are quoted property by property. The Landlord pack page exists so the £561 residential pack has its own address.

The Landlord pack confirmation names the address and the three records. If a second building is mentioned in the same email, it is not silently added to the Landlord pack. Each address is its own Landlord pack booking or its own written quote.

After the Landlord pack papers are emailed, questions about a code on the report are answered against that report. We do not rewrite a failed item into a pass. A follow-on repair is a new instruction with its own price, not a line discovered on the Landlord pack invoice.

A landlord using the Landlord pack is often between tenants and wants the papers before the inventory. The Landlord pack visit can be on an empty house, and we say if the power is off because an EICR needs supply. Furniture still in the rooms is noted so the Landlord pack report does not pretend a socket was accessible when a wardrobe covered it. The landlord, not an unnamed caller, is the person who accepts the £561 scope.

Keys for a Landlord pack are collected and returned the same day. If a tenant is still in residence, the Landlord pack appointment is the time they agreed, and we leave when that window ends even if a loft hatch was locked. The follow-up is another Landlord pack visit or a separate repair quote, booked in writing, not an open-ended promise made on the doorstep.
